To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

mRNA from both unstimulated and stimulated pig lymphocytes has similar ability to direct protein synthesis in cell-free systems, but that cell-free systems from unstimultated lymphocytes have lower efficiency in translating added mRNA.
mRNA is synthesized by unstimulated pig and human lymphocytes and that this mRNA is translated in vitro in a range of different cell-free systems.
the messenger RNA (mRNA) from unstimulated (resting) lymphocytes is as effective as the mRNA from activated lymphocytes in directing protein synthesis in cell-free systems and in the intact cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the regulation of the expression of lymphocyte-specific genes.
the regulation of protein synthesis in lymphocytes and the results indicate that the rate of protein synthesis may be regulated at the level of the messenger RNA.
the study of the mechanism of lymphocyte activation by mitogens and the elucidation of the role of the lymphocyte genome in the immune response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mRNA of activated lymphocytes is more efficiently translated in cell-free systems than is the mRNA of unstimulated lymphoblasts.

the rate of translation of lymphocyte mRNA is stimulated by the activation process, but the degree of activation is not sufficient to account for the observed increase in the rate of protein synthesis in activated lymphocytes.
the ability of lymphocyte poly(A)+ RNA to direct translation is unaltered by phytohaemgagglutinin stimulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, although the messenger RNA from unstimulated cells is fully functional, it is less efficient than that from phytohaegmglutinin-affected lymphocytes.
the ability of the mRNA from unstimulated cells to support protein synthesis is not altered by the addition of phytohaemgglutinin to the culture medium.
, in the absence of any evidence to the contrary, the translational machinery is not altered by phytohaem-agglutinin treatment of lymphocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mRNA isolated from unstimulation and stimulated lymphocytes are functionally equivalent.

the mRNA isolated from unstimu- lated lymphocytes is not inherently inactive in the wheat- germl cell-free system, and the low level of protein syn- thesis obtained with such mRNA preparations is not due to a failure to remove endogenous inhibitors.
the cell-free translation of mRNA isolated from lymphocytes is a valid and sensitive method of measuring changes in mRNA activity.
